subject: Math
text_verbatim: Chapter 1 Numberland Adventures: Up to 999 Then numbers with 4 hundreds: Both have 3 tens Compare ones: 2 and 8 So: 432 then 438 Numbers in ascending order: 108, 120, 192, 432, 438 Practice Questions Now, arrange the above numbers in descending order. Descending numbers means arranging numbers from the largest to the smallest numbers. _________, _________, _________, _________, _________. Discovery Playground Work with your partner and do the following: 1. Make the largest possible 3-digit number using the numbers in the basket. 9 8 3 7 2. Make the smallest possible 3-digit number using the numbers in the basket. 6 2 1 5 3. Make a 3-digit number starting with 4. 1 3 4 9 4 12

exercises.label: Ordering worked example (ascending, part 2): 432 vs 438 (same hundreds and tens)
exercises.instruction_verbatim: Then numbers with 4 hundreds: Both have 3 tens. Compare ones: 2 and 8. So: 432 then 438.

exercises.label: Practice Questions: arrange in descending order
exercises.instruction_verbatim: Now, arrange the above numbers in descending order. Descending numbers means arranging numbers from the largest to the smallest numbers. _____, _____, _____, _____, _____.

exercises.label: Discovery Playground 1: largest 3-digit number from basket {9,8,3,7}
exercises.instruction_verbatim: Make the largest possible 3-digit number using the numbers in the basket.
exercises.answer_key: 987 (pick the 3 largest digits, 9-8-7, in descending order; the basket has 4 digits but only a 3-digit number is being made, so the smallest available digit, 3, is left unused).

exercises.label: Discovery Playground 2: smallest 3-digit number from basket {6,2,1,5}
exercises.instruction_verbatim: Make the smallest possible 3-digit number using the numbers in the basket.
exercises.answer_key: 125 (pick the 3 smallest digits, 1-2-5, in ascending order; 6 is left unused).

exercises.label: Discovery Playground 3: 3-digit number starting with 4, from basket {1,3,4,9}
exercises.instruction_verbatim: Make a 3-digit number starting with 4. [answer boxes: 4, _, _]
exercises.answer_key: Open-ended: the '4' box is pre-filled; the last two boxes are filled with any 2 of the remaining 3 basket digits {1, 3, 9} in any order (e.g. 413, 419, 431, 439, 491, 493 are all valid 3-digit numbers starting with 4). Not a single fixed answer.

illustrations.description: Small character icon reused beside the ordering-lesson text (top of page), matching the icon on the previous page.
Blue circular telescope icon next to 'Discovery Playground' heading (same icon as printed page 7).
Small graduation-cap outline icon next to 'Work with your partner and do the following:'.
Q1: a teal/green shopping-basket icon containing 4 numbers arranged 2x2 (9 top-left, 8 top-right, 3 bottom-left, 7 bottom-right), beside 3 empty answer boxes in a row.
Q2: a teal/green shopping-basket icon containing 4 numbers arranged 2x2 (6 top-left, 2 top-right, 1 bottom-left, 5 bottom-right), beside 3 empty answer boxes in a row.

Q3: a teal/green shopping-basket icon containing 4 numbers arranged 2x2 (1 top-left, 3 top-right, 4 bottom-left, 9 bottom-right), beside 3 answer boxes where the first box is pre-filled with '4' and the remaining 2 boxes are empty.
illustrations.pedagogical_role: digit-arrangement exercise (number starting with a given digit)

visual_layout_notes: Top of page completes the ascending-order worked example from the previous page and states the ascending list. 'Discovery Playground' section (telescope icon) has 3 partner activities, each a teal basket icon holding 4 digits next to a row of empty digit-boxes (Q3's first box is pre-filled with '4').
